card.name: The Brimstone Pit
card.interpretation: I read the site as a giant meteor crater sculpted into the land, the look as a hellish evil lair in an infernal style (nether brick, blackstone, lava glow), and the purpose as a working mining facility. "Repurposed" is kept as the idea that the crater is reused by a dark master, though I added no backstory. The program centres on an overseer's keep on the rim, with foundry, crushers, mine head and barracks down the slopes.
assumptions: Size M, about 10 buildings, fitting a 64-block claim radius.
No tavern or chapel beyond a dark shrine, since it is an evil lair.
Placement is searched for a spot with room for the crater.
Story left empty since none was given beyond 'repurposed'.

program.notes: Jagged dark fortress on the crater rim overlooking the pit; lava-lit windows, spikes, banners.
Smelts ore with lava channels and chimneys; glows red, vents smoke.
Hoppers, pistons and grindstones processing meteor ore; sits on terraces.
Winch and scaffold headframe over the central shaft at the crater floor.
Cramped blackstone bunks with iron bars, set into the crater slope.
Dark altar to the lair's master, nether brick, soul fire and skulls.
Stockpiles of ingots and raw ore behind iron doors and guarded.

log.text: Described as: giant meteor crater, hellish evil lair

card.name: Smugglers' Cove

site.text: carved into sea cliffs, with tunnels cut into the rock and hidden docks at the waterline

style.text: lantern-lit tunnels, damp stone, weathered dark timber, rope and barrels, hidden and shadowy

purpose.text: smugglers' cove for hiding contraband and ships, with hidden docks

card.interpretation: Site: a cove cut into sea cliffs, with tunnels in the rock and docks at the waterline. Style: lantern-lit, damp stone and dark timber, kept shadowy and hidden. Purpose: a smugglers' hideout for ships and contraband. No castle or keep appears in the buildings. I made it medium-sized with about ten buildings, one centrepiece tavern, and the existing sea cliffs used rather than reshaped.
assumptions: Size is M, since none was given.
Terrain uses existing sea cliffs (find) rather than sculpting.
No backstory was given, so none was added.
Location is searched for, since the player did not say spawn or here.

program.notes: Cliff-hollow tavern and meeting hall above the main dock; lantern-lit, with a hidden back exit.
Timber piers tucked in sea caves, with mooring posts and lanterns.
Cave storage packed with barrels, crates and chests; one has a false wall.
Bunks and chests carved into tunnel walls.
Cliff-top lookout disguised among rocks to signal incoming ships.
Trades ship supplies and stolen goods from a tunnel alcove.

log.text: Described as: carved into sea cliffs, with tunnels cut into the rock and hidden docks at the waterline, lantern-lit tunnels, damp stone, weathered dark timber, rope and barrels, hidden and shadowy

card.name: Greywater Hamlet

site.text: small hamlet on the shore of a lake, with docks reaching into the water

style.text: weathered grey timber, nets drying on racks, smoke from a smokehouse

purpose.text: small fishing hamlet: catching, drying and smoking fish for the village

card.interpretation: You asked for a small lakeside fishing hamlet. I took the site as a waterfront on existing lake shore, the style as rustic with weathered grey timber, and the purpose as fishing with drying and smoking of the catch. The program is about six buildings: a smokehouse as the centrepiece, three cottages, a net-drying rack area and a boathouse with a pier. No backstory was given, so none is added.
assumptions: Size S because it is a small hamlet.
Density low for a sparse hamlet.
Location is searched for a suitable lake, since you did not say near spawn or here.
Rustic style template used for the weathered timber look.
Terrain left as found, with no sculpting.

program.notes: Grey plank walls, chimney with constant campfire smoke, hanging fish racks inside; the hamlet's centrepiece.
Weathered grey timber, low roofs, barrels and oars by the door.
Open frames of fence and string-like cobweb-free netting near the shore.
Open to the water, boats moored beside a pier.

log.text: Described as: a village on stilts over a swamp, boardwalks linking platforms above murky water, mossy, crooked, weathered timber, leaning stilts, hanging vines, moss and mud, dim lantern light
Described as: small hamlet on the shore of a lake, with docks reaching into the water, weathered grey timber, nets drying on racks, smoke from a smokehouse
